> **Status: Proposal; target LayerFS 0.1.7; not a released contract.**
> Recommendation recorded 2026-10-07 after the owner's discussion of per-tool-call mounting, multiple Workspaces per sandbox and whether a redesign is needed. Creating this issue performs no product change or measurement and claims no new speedup or completed S8 acceptance.

Parent implementation tracker: [#307](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/307). Design: [#303](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/303). Related explanations: [#308 — sandbox cache design](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/308), [#309 — Workspace filesystem view](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/309). Related engine/lifetime work: [#310](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/310), [#311](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/311). Optional component optimizations remain in [#313](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/313).

## Problem and recommendation

LayerFS supports fresh Workspace mounts for individual tool calls as well as long-lived Workspaces serving many sequential or concurrent calls. A sandbox can serve several Workspaces. Recreating the daemon, reopening the Store, allocating a private immutable cache or initializing a new overlay database for every mount would discard useful reuse and add bootstrap cost.

Complete S8 using the existing architecture: keep the daemon and its shared owners alive; create and retire each Workspace/mount independently. An architectural redesign is not selected. Implement and prove the native lifecycle and coherent cache integration before tuning optional mechanisms. Completion of #313 is not a prerequisite for starting S8, and this issue creates no new pre-S8 gate.

## Current architecture and evidence boundary

- One shared global Store holds immutable content and mutable history. Daemons open it directly from the shared in-VM volume; the host performs Init/seal/install and then sends control commands. The host-mediated data path is retired.
- One local `overlay.sqlite` belongs to each daemon. Mutable metadata, payload, operation records and custody are Workspace-prefixed. Closing one Workspace does not close the shared database.
- The current Store adapter owns a fixed read-handle pool and one bounded `CanonicalCache`. Operation-scoped clients receive that same cache owner; their authority and original provider failures remain separate.
- Bounded root binding, warm object reuse, multiple Workspaces, short-job engine fairness, logical control close and automatic reclamation have scoped pre-S8 proofs. Those proofs do not establish native FUSE readiness, Bash lifecycle, per-mount kernel coherence or a before/after mounted speedup.
- The legacy FUSE directory remains excluded from the active core workspace at the source pin below. Existing files or component examples are not a built S8 replacement.

Relevant local evidence is `core/docs/issues/307/PRE-S8-COMPLETION-20261007.md`, `PRE-S8-F6-F7-20261007.md`, `PRE-S8-F13-20261007.md` and `PRE-S8-RESOURCE-GROWTH-RESULTS-20261007.md`. Warm-bind proof means zero **object** Store demands; a coherent history snapshot and local binding work are still paid. These are local reviewed paths, not remotely published source/evidence links.

## Cache and ownership lifetimes

| Resource | Owner and key | Across Workspace unmount/remount |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Authenticated immutable objects | One daemon Store/cache owner; exact object ID within the allowed Store/profile/authority context | Retain eligible entries until bounded eviction or daemon shutdown. Different roots reuse only identical canonical objects. Never key by pathname or branch name alone. |
| Store sessions and physical-reader caches | Fixed daemon-owned writer/read sessions | Reuse across bindings; no per-mount reopen or reader-pool growth. |
| Overlay connection and pager | One daemon SQL owner | Keep initialized; Workspace namespaces retain independent mutable visibility and custody. Pager allowance is not a whole-process memory bound. |
| Kernel dentries, attributes and file pages | Individual FUSE mount/connection | Fresh mount has fresh kernel state. Stable inode serials do not transplant the prior connection's cache. |
| Requests, open handles, lookup references, read plans and mount buffers | Exact Workspace/mount/operation owners | Fence admission and release according to their actual lifetimes; track remaining ownership and cleanup debt. |
| `.git/index`, dependencies, application caches and outputs | Ordinary filesystem data in the selected root and local overlay | Reuse committed artifacts through the next selected root. Cache retention does not carry uncommitted mutations into a new Workspace. |

Example: Workspace A reads canonical object D, then terminates. Workspace B on another branch can reuse retained D if its authorized root references D. A changed version E is distinct. A's local edits never alter B's base view. The daemon cache may survive even when no Workspaces are currently mounted; it need not retain D indefinitely.

## S8 priorities

### 1. Reuse daemon infrastructure and make fresh attachment bounded

- Retain one Store binding, fixed readers, immutable cache and initialized overlay across tool calls, including zero-mounted-Workspace intervals.
- Bind a coherent selected root using bounded root checks, then attach the native mount. Do not scan/copy/materialize the base, restore dependencies or prefetch the whole tree in mount setup.
- Keep process lifetime, Workspace lifetime, Exec duration and Commit cadence independent. Support several concurrent Workspaces and both fresh-per-call and persistent operation.
- Account for actual session receive buffers and workers per live mount. Negotiating 128 KiB requests does not prove 128 KiB receive-buffer allocation. Avoid duplicate first-party state; retain the pinned public dependency boundary.

### 2. Complete coherent kernel caching

- Start from the existing promoted candidate: 60-second entry/attribute TTL and cached reads using KEEP_CACHE, with kernel writeback off and permissions retained. These remain candidates until their mounted correctness/resource proofs pass.
- Long TTL and page retention mainly reduce repeated callbacks within one mount; daemon immutable object/metadata reuse supplies the cross-mount mechanism.
- Prove hard-link aliases, replacement rename, writes, shrink/regrow tails, stale attribute replies, symlinks and supported dirty-mmap/kernel-origin request semantics. TTL expiry is not a correctness mechanism.
- Preserve valid caches across a known base install only when the complete visible names, bytes, links, metadata and inode identity are unchanged and later active writes remain visible.
- Remove routine WRITE invalidation only after the corresponding coherence and kernel ordering proof. Notification handling must not deadlock the reply or hold the SQL owner.
- Cheap owning file-length delivery already exists. A complete additional immutable-attribute cache is separate integration/optimization work; do not claim it already exists or cache mutable stat results without version validation.

### 3. Keep concurrent requests runnable

- Connect FUSE request/reply ownership to the existing bounded fair engine. Park requests awaiting readiness without monopolizing dispatch workers or retaining Workspace locks across SQL service/base acquisition.
- Prove unrelated access progresses when both initial workers encounter guarded requests; test simultaneous activity across Workspaces.
- Preserve short atomic mutation publication and reply ordering. Never hold a Store/overlay writer or global gate across a file, Exec, Save or Commit.
- Readiness parking is distinct from retry. A failed Store write returns its typed Busy/original failure without automatic replay. Terminal control unmount may refuse while ownership remains; ordinary filesystem contention must not become refusal-based coherence.

### 4. Release mount state without discarding reusable owners

- Terminal unmount fences callbacks, detaches the native session and joins/disposes its owned workers and buffers. Track kernel lookup/FORGET references separately from open/RELEASE references.
- Use targeted ownership updates instead of repeated whole-state collection. Preserve retained orphan reads and exact lost-reply/unknown custody.
- Bash exit is not a fence for descendants, descriptors, mappings or pending requests. Unmount must obey the actual ownership contract; no implicit Commit, automatic command timeout or guessed cleanup.
- Release the Workspace namespace when its original owners permit it. Let bounded automatic reclamation progress during live/idle activity, report terminal completion and remaining physical debt separately, and preserve progress in other Workspaces.
- Closing a Workspace must not flush the shared immutable cache, recreate the overlay or delete global history. Global physical history/storage and OS cache growth must not be relabeled as a local ownership leak.

## Prospective native proof coverage

Select and register concrete cases through the owning #307/harness workflow; this list does not freeze a new measurement campaign or numeric threshold.

- [ ] Fresh mount -> read/stat/ordinary Exec -> explicit terminal unmount over a complete root, with bounded binding and actual native resource closure.
- [ ] Repeated mounts on one root reuse retained objects while every mount's kernel state starts independently. Record history/local work as well as object calls.
- [ ] Nearby-branch mounts reuse identical objects and isolate changed versions/local edits; retained authorized reads remain correct across publication/install.
- [ ] Several simultaneous Workspaces, parked requests and concurrent cold/warm reads make progress under declared credits and reader capacity.
- [ ] Cache pressure and eviction preserve correctness and unrelated progress. Shared dispatch fairness does not by itself prove fair cache residency.
- [ ] Persistent same-mount calls retain coherent caches through writes, rename, truncate and known install; record S10 dependencies for complete live Commit normalization.
- [ ] Repeated attach/detach and cancellation/teardown release original request/handle/lookup/session ownership, with bounded reclamation progress and exact unknown outcomes.
- [ ] Full oracles cover the affected byte, namespace, alias and metadata semantics; component cache-hit counts do not close mounted acceptance.

Record native request counts, Store batches/misses, copied/decoded bytes, SQL/VM/row/page work where relevant, queue/service waits, session worker/buffer ownership, cleanup work and storage. Keep Rust allocations, SQLite pager/journal, FUSE/kernel pages and OS file cache separately scoped; a bounded cache allowance is not a bound on the whole sandbox. Timed comparisons require equal declared/enforced cache state, existing budgets, one sample per selected case/arm and append-only receipts. Warm cross-call reuse must be labeled warm, not credited to a cold phase. Report unsupported exact peaks/physical attribution explicitly; invent no acceptance ceiling.

## Documentation reconciliation and deferred refinements

- [ ] Update #308's implementation reconciliation: shared Store cache wiring has advanced since its October 5 source review. Preserve original source pins and distinguish completed seams from native qualification.
- [ ] Add the current direct Store diagram/explanation to #309 and mark the October 5 host-mediated diagram superseded. Preserve the owner's requested original diagram as historical material.
- [ ] Keep #313's narrower cache-copy, pack-search, partial-cell and batching candidates separate. Evaluate them from actual costs; they need not delay starting S8.

Negative-entry tuning, adaptive READDIRPLUS, FLUSH elision, copy-file-range reuse, larger requests, additional dispatch concurrency, miss coalescing and alternate eviction policy remain optional investigations. No new private per-Workspace cache, mutable mirror, database layout or native session architecture is selected without a demonstrated requirement.

## Execution constraints and compatibility

Global Store execution is explicitly Disposable / WAL / synchronous=OFF only. Retained Durable implementation may compile; all Durable execution is `NOT_RUN — disabled by owner until explicit reauthorization`. The daemon overlay remains separate MEMORY/OFF/EXCLUSIVE; no fsync is introduced on Workspace backing. Linux Store files require the in-VM named volume or native container filesystem, never the repository host-share mount.

Preserve current canonical identity/public boundaries, acknowledged writes, permission checks, current Branch publication policy, original failure/unknown custody and no automatic retry. Use existing dependencies and only the already authorized fuser timestamp patch. Follow the existing scoped locked build-before-test, bounded-test, Clippy/fmt/boundary and exact production-LOC commit rules for any later implementation. This recommendation performs no builds/tests/measurements and does not reopen historical receipts or authorize remote source pushes.
